Mr. A. N. M. Gaziul Hoque, Advocate with Mr. Syed Golam Mostafa Advocate and Mrs. Umme Kulsum Begum, Advocate ------ For the appellants.

parties:
Dr. Ishaq Ali and others ------Appellants.
Vs.
The State ------ Respondent.
full_judgment: 7. Now, on careful scrutiny of the evidence as narrated above it is found that there is no evidence of any witnesses as to concealment of the dead body of the victim Abdus Samad save and except the evidence of P.Ws. 1,2,3, and 6 as to the alleged recovery of his dead-body. P.Ws. 1, 2 and 3 are all the Police personnel’s and P.W.6 is the Magistrate who are said to be present at the time and place of the alleged recovery of the dead-body of the victim. According to the evidence of these witnesses the dead-body of the victim was recovered from inside a gunny bag which was kept concealed beneath the earth in the bank of the river Tulshi-Gonga at Shimultali. None of these witnesses has seen the act of concealment of the dead body of the victim in the bank of the said river. Now, all the accused appellants have been convicted and sentenced under Section 201 of the Penal Code for screening evidence of the case of murder i.e. for concealing the dead body of the victim Abdus Samad. It may be noticed that there is a confessional statement of accused Idris under Section 164 Cr.P.C. recorded by the Magistrate P.W.6 which has been marked as Ext. 9 and from the said confessional statement it appears that accused Idris was asked by these accused appellants particularly appellant Dr. Ishaq Ali to conceal the dead body of the victim, but he expressed his inability first to do it, but ultimately he along with some others carried the dead body in a gunny bag and concealed the same beneath the earth in the bank of the river Tulshi Gonga on 12.1.90 and thereafter he was asked to keep the matter suppressed. But when he was arrested by police on 7.2.90 he however disclose that he along with others had concealed the dead-body of the victim which he subsequently brought out when he was asked by the Police to do so and then identified the same as the dead body of the victim Abdus Samad. So in the said confessional statement of accused Idris Ali we find some sort of involvement of these accused appellants with the matter of concealment of dead-body of the victim Abdus Samad. Now, it has been contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that there is no other reliable evidence as against the accused appellants to implicate them in the matter of either concealment or recovery of the dead body of the said victim. It has been further contended on behalf of the appellants that confessional statement of a co-accused namely Idris can not be the sole basis of conviction of these co-accused appellants and the confessional statement of co-accused Idris at best can lend assurance to any other evidence as against the other accused appellants. In support of this contention the learned Advocate for the appellants has relied on some decisions namely in the case of Lutfun Nahar Begum Vs. The State reported in 27 DLR(AD) 29 and also in the case of Amir Hossain Vs. State reported in 37 DLR(AD) 139 and also in the case of the case of Bhuboni Saha Vs. The King reported in 2 DLR(PC) 39 of course, apart from this, it has been further contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the alleged confession of co-accused Idris was subsequently retracted and the same was also not true and voluntary as the same was made under decrees and torture by the Police. Now, as accused Idris who has been convicted and sentenced along with these appellants under Section 201 of the Penal Code has not presented any appeal before us, we are not interested to decide the propriety or legality of his conviction and sentence and we are also not interested to ascertain the circumstances under which he made the said confession, also whether his confession was true or voluntary. We are rather on the question as to how his alleged confession could be used as against these appellants for convicting them when there is no other reliable evidence against them as to the murder of the victim or the concealment or recovery of the dead body of the victim. From the above settled principles, even if the confessional statement of accused Idris is found to be true and voluntary still his confession cannot be used against these appellants who are co-accused in the case as the basis convicting them when there is no other evidence against them. So far P.W.4 Bilkis @ Pakhi the wife of the victim is concerned it is found that she made some statements against these appellants in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate in respect of concealment of the dead body of the victim. But in her evidence in court she has made a serious departure and denied her statement before the Magistrate as well as before the Police alleging the same to be a product of threat, torture and confinement. She has only come to say that her husband on the fateful night came out from the house but did not return thereafter and since then she was not aware of his whereabouts. Apart from that we find from the charge as framed in this case that the allegation of concealment of the dead-body of the alleged victim is to the effect that the accused persons called out the victim from his hut and after killing him his dead body was kept concealed within a heap of straw on the court-yard of Jamiruddin, father-in-law of the victim. This charge does not appear to have been amended and ultimately the charge, of course under Section 302/34 failed and the accused appellants have been found guilty and convicted under Section 201 of the Penal Code for concealing the dead body of the victim no4 within the heap of straw in the court yeard of Jamiruddin but for concealment of the same beneatdh the earth in the hank of the river Tulshi-Gongs that means at a different place and in a different manner. This is also a matter to be looked into before convicting the accused appellants under Section 201 of the Penal Code. In the present case there is no evidence to show that the alleged dead-body of the victim was kept concealed within on the heap of straw of the court-yard of the father-in-law of the victim as alleged in the charge. Mr. Gaziul Hoque the learned Advocate has also seriously raised the question as to the identity of the dead body of the alleged victim Abdus Samad from the medical report and also from the evidence of the doctor P.W.5 According to the learned Advocate, the identity of the dead body of the victim Abdus Samad has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt. However, it transpires that the dead body alleged to have been recovered from the bank of the river Tulshi Gonga was on a decomposed condition, of course, some parts of it were decomposing not fully decomposed and when the alleged body was recovered, it is in the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, 3 and another that some people came and recognised or identified the same to the of victim Abdus samad, but nobody has specifically named any of the identifiers save and except in the deposition of P.W. 6 it appears that one Yunus Ali actually recognised the dead-body of the victim Abdus Samad with the help of some cloths namely pant, shirt, sweater etc. and particularly with the help of a tabiz bearing the writing 'Allah' on it. Of course these alamats have been seized proved and marked as the Exts. but the said Yunus Ali who is said to have identified the dead-body of the victim with the help of these alamats has not been produced in court by the prosecution in this case as a witness and it also does not appear that the said Yunus Ali was even cited as a charge-sheet witness for reasons unknown. So non production of this material witness Yunus Ali and also some other witnesses named in the charge-sheet particularly the sweepers namely C.S. witness No. 6 Sree Krishna. C.S witness No. 7 Sree Shontosh C.S. witness No. 8 Kishore and C.S. witness No. 9 Modni of Jaipurhat Sweeper Colony who are said to have handed the dead body of the victim at the time of its recovery, has caused serious adverse effect on the prosecution case and so far non-production of Yunus Ali in particular has given rise to an adverse presumption under Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against the prosecution case specially in respect of the identity of the dead body of the deceased victim vide decision in the case of Alkas Mia Vs. State in 25 DLR 398. Now, question may arise as to why these appellants would be falsely implicated in this case by the prosecution and also by co-accused Idris in his confession. From a scrutiny of the records and the statement of accused appellant Dr. Ishaq under Section 342 Cr.P.C., we find that he has made a short but a precise statement to the effect that there was a dacoity in the village Shampur and in that dacoity some dacoits were injured and he made some medical treatment to some of them for which the police implicated him as an accused in that case but he was ultimately in that case acquitted. Further he has stated that with co-acquitted Idris, he has some dispute over lands and as such enmity. He of course has also stated that he was not aware of anything of the occurrence. So from the above, false involvement of the appellant particularly Dr. Ishaq Ali cannot he Brushed aside. Mr. Enamul Haque the learned Advocate for the State however in view of the above state of evidence in the case and the position of law finds it difficult to press for upholding the conviction of the appellants. Now, having considered all aspects of the case and the materials on record, we are of the view that the prosecution has not been able to establish the charge under Section 201 of the penal Code as against these appellants beyond all reasonable doubt and in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to give them benefit of doubt and as such acquittal.
